title: A bead stack is a measurement of the PSF
text:
A sub-resolution bead is a point, so its image is the point-spread function of this objective, this medium and this alignment. The tool fits a three-dimensional Gaussian to each bead and reports the widths in nanometres: that is what you compare with the PSF calculator, and what a deconvolution or a super-resolution reconstruction needs.

Five steps.

title: Load a stack
text: Load a 3-D TIFF of beads, or press Demo stack for a generated stack whose answer is known (five beads, true FWHM 424 nm laterally and 2120 nm axially).

await.hint: Press Demo stack (or Load stack to use your own file).

title: Say what a pixel and a slice are worth
text: Pixel (nm) and Z step (nm) turn the fitted sigmas into physical widths. They are the only way the fit knows the scale, so a wrong value gives a confident answer in the wrong units.

title: Find the beads
text: Detect marks the bright regions that are large enough and far enough from each other to be single beads. If it finds none, lower Px/frame or Min area; if it finds hot pixels, raise Min area.

title: Fit them all, then read the spread
text: Fit all fits every bead and lists failures too. One bead is an anecdote: the scatter over the beads is the real error of the PSF width. Then look at the x, y and z profile tabs: the data should follow the red Gaussian.
